comment: Interview claims after the 2026-11-09 audit. A 'safe' claim is backed by tests that must pass (checked by scripts/audit-report.ts); 'unsafe' claims say why not. Synthetic data throughout: never present a number as Moxie's.

claims.claim: Ingestion is exactly-once: a record version is stored once however often it is delivered, and a re-observed version that changes live rows still wakes reconciliation.

evidence.name: delivering the same batch three times changes nothing after the first

claims.claim: Sync workers are fenced: a worker that lost its claim cannot overwrite another's results, a request key is idempotent, and a kick is never lost.

evidence.name: B-2: a kick that arrives while the drain dispatches events is not lost

claims.claim: Domain events use a transactional outbox with snapshot coverage: a late-committing change is never lost, and a burst of batches costs one recomputation.

evidence.name: an event whose transaction commits after a run started is not covered by that run
a consumer runs only for changes its last run did not see

claims.claim: No stored record changes without propose → rolled-back dry run → approval by another role → one verified execution; the legacy replay API refuses commits.
A fix is verified against the ledger: ad spend, raw events, CRM customers, invoiced and collected are conserved, and re-executing returns the stored result.
Budget signals refuse to rank channels on broken data, including unmapped spend that produced a branch's customers.

evidence.name: blocks the budget signal while open

claims.claim: Collected revenue in the seeded scenario equals the generated payment ground truth to the cent.

evidence.name: collected revenue equals the generated payment ground truth to the cent

claims.claim: Branch and brand scope is enforced on the server for every read and write, and an out-of-scope id reads as missing.

evidence.name: a branch partner cannot read another branch
an out-of-scope incident reads as missing
a branch partner cannot fetch another branch through any tool

claims.claim: The AI investigator cannot write SQL or act: fixed tools with strict schemas, every citation must come from this run's tool output, record text is delimited as data, and it can only create proposals that still need a dry run and approval.
A production build is not a demo: without DEMO_MODE=1 the role cookie is ignored and the role picker and CRM mock are off.
The FieldRoutes client follows the documented search → get pattern: 50k search paging, ≤1,000-record gets, office-scoped, fails loudly on ignored filters, and survives the autumn clock change.

evidence.name: pages searches at the cap and batches gets at the limit

claims.claim: The four-minute B09 path reproduces on every fresh seed, and every number it quotes is asserted in the browser.
It has been run against a real FieldRoutes tenant, CallRail account or Google Ads account.
claims.why: Never. Only the in-repo mock and synthetic world; no credentials were used.

claims.claim: The FieldRoutes connector is production-ready.
claims.why: Mapper deviations G1–G10 are open (Pacific-time datetimes, isInitial, templateType, payment applications); deletes/merges (G-7) and late payment changes (G-8) are not detected; the repeated-hour stale-version case is open.

claims.claim: It sends conversions to Google, or retracts cancelled ones.
claims.why: Dry run only; no network code. Data Manager cannot retract; cancelled plans are simply not sent. Enhanced conversions for leads, gbraid/wbraid and consent are not implemented.

claims.claim: It respects Google's click window.
claims.why: Approximated from the lead time with a fixed 90 days (F-3).

claims.claim: The AI investigator was evaluated with a real model.
claims.why: The model path is tested with a scripted client; the deterministic investigator is what ran. No API key was used.

claims.claim: It has authentication.
claims.why: Demo roles without passwords, server-enforced; production needs SSO claims (ADR-11, ADR-20).

claims.claim: CI passes on GitHub.
claims.why: No GitHub Actions run has been observed for the repository; the CI workflow has only been reproduced locally.

claims.claim: Branch CAC is unambiguous.
claims.why: Spend follows the marketing branch, customers the servicing office (D-2, documented, not resolved).

claims.claim: Moxie has this problem / uses Local Services Ads / any number here is Moxie's.
claims.why: All data is synthetic; the problem is a hypothesis from public signals.
